luna.identity_reason: The supplied Europe PMC metadata links this preprint reciprocally to PMID 42507152. The titles differ in wording, but the author names match, and both identify an adolescent study of vitamin B12, restless legs syndrome, and poor sleep quality. The supplied preprint also names the linked journal version. This extraction uses only the supplied v1 preprint, not the journal full text.
luna.reason: The preprint reports continuous PSQI scores across serum vitamin B12 categories in a cross-sectional adolescent sample, so the requested exposure and outcome are present. It reports category-level PSQI values but no estimate-specific contrast, confidence interval, standard error, or exact P value for PSQI by vitamin B12 status. No effect was derived. The narrative claim that the deficient group had the poorest sleep scores conflicts with the Table 4 total-score values, so the direction is unresolved.
unresolved_fields: No estimate-specific PSQI contrast, confidence interval, standard error, or exact P value for the vitamin B12 category comparison is reported.
The Results narrative says the deficient group had the poorest sleep scores, whereas Table 4 lists a higher PSQI total score in the sufficient group than in the deficient or borderline groups.

extraction.comparison_direction: No pairwise contrast specified. Table 4 lists categories in deficient (<200 pg/mL), borderline (200–300 pg/mL), sufficient (>300 pg/mL) order, with PSQI values 9, 9, and 10.3, respectively. Higher PSQI scores indicate poorer sleep quality.

extraction.p_value_provenance: No PSQI-by-vitamin-B12-category P value reported. The Results' p < 0.05 refers to RLS frequency, not the requested PSQI contrast.
extraction.ci_provenance: No confidence interval for PSQI scores by vitamin B12 category reported.

gemini.identity_reason: Preprint PPR1167312 shares the identical author team (Kubra Boztepe, Nurten Zarif Ozkan, Nesibe Kubra Gol, Ozgur Pirgon), study setting (Süleyman Demirel University Faculty of Medicine), adolescent cohort (146 patients aged 10-16), and research focus on vitamin B12, restless legs syndrome, and sleep quality as published PMID 42507152, and the preprint explicitly links to the published article DOI 10.1007/s00431-026-07281-y.
gemini.reason: The study evaluates serum vitamin B12 levels and PSQI sleep quality scores in 146 adolescents and provides group sample sizes, means, and SDs across three vitamin B12 categories (<200 pg/mL: 9 ± 3.4, n=40; 200–300 pg/mL: 9 ± 2.8, n=35; >300 pg/mL: 10.3 ± 1.2, n=71) in Table 4. However, no comparative effect size (beta or mean difference), confidence interval, standard error, or statistical p-value is reported for this association. Per the outcome-scope safeguard, missing quantities require retention rather than exclusion, making the study eligible but not quantitatively poolable.
